# GPU enablement — round 3: resizable BAR and the 64-bit window

Same author (Opus 5.5/high) and worktree, on top of **`8d6dba9`** (passed Sol R3; placed in Fleet). The owner-approved real rehearsal `20261020T003504Z-f08a` ended `preflight-failed/10` with nothing changed. The host has resizable BAR on: BAR1 is 32 GiB, plus BAR3 32 MiB, for 33,587,200 KiB of 64-bit prefetchable memory. The guest's OVMF 64-bit window is 32 GiB, and the old fixed 8 GiB limit refused. The coordinator decided to keep ReBAR, enlarge the guest window, and avoid a host reboot. Preparation only: no ask, host, VM, package or service change.

**New host script SHA-256: `ca097451d38937001f3ce7a3a97adbe33631b7b04f45a7a96708a5fcf8535c6b`** (was `e3365eb3…92d7`). `worker-gpu.sh`: `4fd1f40ad15833e4c2fbda3cc053bc34d0cecf48efe26637913375355bd32152`. `ask-command.sh` and `webgl-probe.mjs` are unchanged. The full list is in `final-source-sha256.txt`.

| Item | Change | Evidence and tests (all R3 cases fail on `8d6dba9`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Window entry | Attach adds `<sysinfo type='fwcfg'><entry name='opt/ovmf/X-PciMmio64Mb'>N</entry></sysinfo>`, libvirt's **native** element, in preference to `<qemu:commandline>`. Because `attach-device` cannot add `<sysinfo>`, the change is now one `virsh define` of the VM's own `--security-info` inactive XML (passwords kept) with only our entries added or removed. The temp file is root-only, in the host's `/tmp`, and removed at once. | Sources checked (sources in `src/`):<br>• OVMF: edk2 `MemDetect.c` reads `opt/ovmf/X-PciMmio64Mb`, sets `PcdPciMmio64Override` and bypasses the dynamic and classic sizing.<br>• Command line: libvirt 12.2.0 `qemuBuildSysinfoCommandLine` emits exactly `-fw_cfg name=…,string=…`.<br>• Format: `virSysinfoFormatFWCfg` writes `<entry name='…'>V</entry>` on one line.<br>`pcihole64` is not used: it sets only QEMU's ACPI window. Tests: the ReBAR attach gives `attached/0` with the hostdevs and `65536` defined and running; the native sysinfo has no QEMU namespace; no security-info file is left in `/tmp`; the order is shutdown → one define → start. |
| 2. Ownership | "Ours" is now the pair *hostdev sources \| fw_cfg value*. Any other fw_cfg entry, a `file=` blob for our name, any `<qemu:…>` element, or a non-PCI hostdev makes it foreign: refused at preflight, `needs-owner` at recovery. The comparisons strip exactly our hostdevs and our fw_cfg sysinfo. Plans follow the pair, so a dropped fw_cfg entry (Unraid form view) is a `full` re-attach. Detach and every rollback remove both. | Foreign `<qemu:commandline>`, foreign fw_cfg entry, and our name as a `file=` blob: refused for attach and detach. Detach leaves the definition equal to the original. A dropped entry is restored by attach. Start fails with the GPU: rolled back, fw_cfg removed too. libvirt dropping the sysinfo: unexpected, undone, never started half-changed. Another change landing with our define: undone, not attached. The existing rollback, undo-failure and boundary cases were rewritten from `attach-device` to `define` with the same intent. |
| 3. Computed fit | The fixed `MAX_PREF64_KIB` is gone. Window = next power of two ≥ card 64-bit prefetchable + 2 GiB (the other root ports' 256 MiB paddings), minimum 64 GiB; this card gives **65536**. It must end within the CPU's physical address bits once placed above RAM and aligned to its size (host `address sizes`; the CPU is host-passthrough). The window is re-derived at every boundary check. | Sizing basis: edk2 `CalculateResourceAperture` aligns a bridge aperture to the bridge's own 1 MiB, so the GPU port needs 32 GiB + 32 MiB. Tests: the default fixture is now the real host (ReBAR BARs, 39 bits), and preflight reports `X-PciMmio64Mb=65536`. Refused: 36 physical bits; a 256 GiB BAR (a 512 GiB window cannot be addressed); unreadable address bits. |
| 4. `check post` | Finds 10de:2204 in sysfs and requires BAR1 assigned (non-zero, prefetchable) and inside a top-level `PCI Bus 0000:00` window of this boot's `/proc/iomem`, read as root. It reports the window and, if visible, the `X-PciMmio64Mb` value delivered (`qemu_fw_cfg`; a WARN otherwise). The Linux window is **not** expected to be 64 GiB: QEMU's ACPI window starts at the lowest 64-bit BAR, so containment is what is checked. | BAR1 inside the window passes, with the window and value shown. BAR1 unassigned, BAR1 outside every window, and iomem unreadable each FAIL alone. A missing fw_cfg is a WARN when BAR1 is placed. Every post case now regenerates a valid report, so it fails only for its own reason; the old "nvidia-smi failing" case had partly passed because its report was missing. |
| 5. README | New section on resizable BAR and the 64-bit window: mechanism and sources, sizing, ownership, the guest check, the **Unraid form-view** caveat (re-run rehearsal; attach restores it), and **Windows 11 Gaming** probably having the same latent problem (unchanged). Owner decisions (ReBAR kept, BIOS alternative), recovery, undo and "not verified" are updated. | — |
| 6. Tests | Run sequentially in a 1 GiB / zero-swap user scope with `timeout 300s` and a hostile PATH:<br>• **red** — final tests against `8d6dba9`: host 103 pass / 59 fail and guest 58 / 5, including all 21 R3-specific cases. Most other host failures are the expected consequence: the old script refuses the real ReBAR host, as in the live rehearsal.<br>• **final** — exit 0, **162 host + 63 guest + 5 ask + 39 probe = 269 checks**, 169 s on a busy machine. | `initial-failures/r3-cases-against-8d6dba9.log`, `final-suite.log` |

Test-only artifacts fixed along the way:
- the captured fixture ends with an extra blank line that a re-serialized definition does not have, so the tests now compare text as the script does, ignoring trailing newlines;
- the iomem zeroing case now allows the real indented lines;
- the framebuffer case uses the real BAR1 address.

**Still to verify live:**
- that Unraid's OVMF honours the entry and places BAR1 in the window (`check post`);
- that libvirt's re-serialization matches across our define and its undo (otherwise the run backs off truthfully);
- everything already listed in R1-FIX and the README.
